anomalies.observed: On the schematic sheet, the Water Level Sensor/Switches section shows PR1 (LiDAR) connected: VCC to +5V, SDA and SCL to the global I2C_SDA/I2C_SCL labels, and GND to GND.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that PR1 is present but not wired: its pins are typed free, it is marked on_board: no / excluded from board, and the wired water-level sensor is an HC-SR04-style ultrasonic sensor on two GPIOs.

evidence.quote: Water Level Sensor/Switches: PR1 LiDAR ... I2C_SDA, I2C_SCL, +5V, GND
PR1 ... pins are 'free' and it is marked on_board: no / excluded from board; it is not wired into any net
The water-level sensing that is actually wired and actually used by firmware is an HC-SR04-style ultrasonic sensor read on two ESP32 GPIOs

anomalies.impact: The board would have an additional LiDAR device on the main I2C bus instead of the intended ultrasonic water-level interface; a 5V I2C device may also load or level-conflict with the 3.3V I2C bus.

anomalies.observed: In the ATO Valve driver, R12 (10k) is tied from the T5 gate node to GND, while T4 (BT3904 NPN) is used as a common-emitter predriver to that same gate node. There is no pull-up to +3V3 on the ATO valve MOSFET gate.
anomalies.expected: For an NPN common-emitter predriver driving a low-side N-MOSFET, the MOSFET gate should be pulled up to +3V3 (as R5 does for the main pump) so that turning T4 off allows the gate to rise and turn T5 on; alternatively a non-inverting driver topology would be required.

evidence.quote: ATO Valve: R12 10k connected at T5 gate to GND; T4 BT3904 collector to T5 gate
T3 — AON6407 ... ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch ... gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904)

anomalies.impact: The ATO solenoid valve would be unable to turn on, disabling automatic top-off.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains at least two deviations from the intended design: PR1 LiDAR is wired onto the I2C bus even though the spec says it is not connected, and the ATO valve MOSFET gate appears pulled down instead of pulled up, preventing the valve from turning on.
